answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with costly identity: each agent locks a deposit before transacting, slashed if peers prove misbehavior. A single operator spinning up many fake identities pays a real bill for each one, so the delta between one honest agent and a flock of sock puppets becomes the attack's price tag. Reputation accrues slowly through verified work: a raven with a hundred attested jobs carries weight a newborn sparrow cannot fake overnight, and high-value tasks require a minimum score. Sybils can appear, but they start weak and stay expensive.
